title: Multiplying and dividing algebraic fractions
summary: Factor numerators and denominators, cancel common factors, and convert division into multiplication by the reciprocal while respecting restrictions.
objectives: Factor expressions before cancelling common factors.
Multiply algebraic fractions and simplify completely.
Divide algebraic fractions using the reciprocal and state excluded values.

blocks.text: Algebraic fractions follow the same rules as numerical fractions. Before multiplying, factor each numerator and denominator. A factor may be cancelled only when it multiplies the whole numerator and whole denominator.

Terms joined by addition or subtraction cannot be cancelled separately. For example, x/(x+2) cannot be simplified because x is not a factor of the complete denominator. Writing brackets around factored expressions makes valid cancellation visible.

For multiplication, combine numerators and combine denominators. Cross-cancellation is simply cancellation of common factors before those products are formed. Cancelling early keeps coefficients and powers small.
Use index laws on repeated variables: a^m/a^n=a^{m-n} when a≠0. Keep factors in a readable order and place any factor with a negative remaining power in the denominator.

sections.title: Division means multiply by the reciprocal

blocks.text: To divide by an algebraic fraction, multiply by its reciprocal. Reverse the entire divisor, including every factor, then proceed as for multiplication. The divisor itself must not equal zero, and every original denominator must also be non-zero.

Restrictions come from the original expression, even if a factor later cancels. Record excluded values before simplifying. This prevents the simplified expression from appearing defined at a value that was forbidden in the original question.
